title: Iron Man & Hulk: Heroes United
edition: 2013 US Disney animated home-video feature released December 3
synopsis: HYDRA drains energy from Hulk and Abomination to power a reactor. The experiment causes a blackout and releases Zzzax, a living electrical threat.
verdictRationale: In the cemetery, Hulk can move but cannot see, while Tony can see but cannot move freely. Asking for help lets both men protect the other. Their earlier fight makes this change in how they treat each other worth noticing, even amid the long stretches of combat.
ageRationale: Proposed 10+ for repeated fights, Hulk’s temporary blindness and an attack by creatures in a cemetery. Children sensitive to losing sight or being surrounded may find that encounter particularly frightening.
reflection: A child watching Hulk carry Tony might first notice who is stronger. Ask who has to trust a voice he cannot check and who has to entrust his body to another. Each offers a gift while accepting help.

themes.name: Mutual care
themes.evidence: Tony guides Hulk through the cemetery while Hulk supplies the movement Tony lacks. Their dependence gives the partnership its clearest expression.

themes.name: Humility
themes.evidence: Tony credits Hulk with a good idea about Zzzax. The acknowledgment briefly interrupts their rivalry.

themes.name: Exploitation
themes.evidence: HYDRA pits Hulk and Abomination against one another and drains them to fuel its device. Treating captives as resources sets the crisis in motion.

title: Iron Man & Captain America: Heroes United
edition: 2014 US computer-animated feature, 71 minutes, Adrian Pasdar and Roger Craig Smith
synopsis: After sparring over skill and equipment, Tony and Steve face Red Skull, who plans to turn people into soldiers under his control using serum made with Steve’s blood.
verdictRationale: Steve risks annoying a friend to teach him how to fight if his armor fails. Later Tony clears a path for them both. Their friendship offers something to admire, but much of the film’s attention goes to bigger fights and competitive taunts, with little time to consider the people threatened by Red Skull.
ageRationale: Proposed 10+ for near-continuous animated combat and an attempt to bend a captive’s will. Red Skull’s plan to change people against their wishes can be unsettling apart from the physical fighting.
reflection: Steve’s sparring lesson starts an argument because Tony hears a challenge where Steve intends help. Families might consider how to offer correction plainly enough for a friend to hear it, and how to receive it without needing to win.

themes.name: Friendship and correction
themes.evidence: Steve deliberately exposes a weakness during sparring and explains his concern. It gives their opening contest a purpose beyond winning.

themes.name: Cooperation
themes.evidence: Facing troops equipped with stolen abilities, Steve calls for a retreat and Tony clears their route. Each relies on the other’s judgment under pressure.

themes.name: Domination
themes.evidence: Red Skull tries to control Steve’s mind and plans to transform millions into soldiers. The threat to others’ freedom drives the conflict.
